note: The NAMED-MUTANT corpus for a hand-picked subset of the money/gate files the scheduled mutmut/cosmic-ray kill-suite cannot reach (critical-set.json mutation=false: the sovereign-leg apps/sigil files cannot load beside framework, and the engine gates are outside the vigil_core-scoped runner). Each mutant is ONE exact old->new source replacement that breaks ONE named guard, plus the test node(s) that must kill it. tools/mutation/named_mutants.py runs ONE plane per process tree (planes.*.pythonpath is rebuilt from scratch and absolute; the sovereign plane never holds engine/crucible, the offense plane never holds apps/sigil), checks the module imports and the union of each file's named tests is GREEN on the unmutated source, then applies each mutant (the original kept in a <file>.named-mutant.orig sidecar until restored, written atomically with the sha256 of the original in its header; at startup, before the corpus is validated, every corpus file's sidecar is restored if it verifies and refused, leaving source and sidecar as found, if it does not), checks the mutant still imports, runs only its named tests (-x), and always restores the original bytes and mtime. KILLED means pytest exited 1 AND a named test failed by an assertion (AssertionError or pytest.fail, DID NOT RAISE included); a test failing by any other exception, or failing in its setup or teardown phase (an assertion in a fixture included), is CRASHED; exit 0 is SURVIVED; anything else (a mutant that does not import or compile, a collection/usage error, timeout) is ERROR. Only KILLED is a kill. Run: python tools/mutation/named_mutants.py --plane sovereign|offense [--file <path>] [--mutant <id>]. Wired into .github/workflows/mutation-fuzz.yml (job "named-mutant corpus", scheduled, red on any survivor). Every file here must be a python entry of critical-set.json flagged "named_mutants": true (and vice versa), and every mutant must still apply exactly once, compile and name a real test in its own plane: integration/tests/test_mutation_critical_set.py enforces this on every PR, so a refactor that moves a guard's text must update its mutant in the same PR. A mutant that SURVIVES is a missing test (or dead code): add the test, never weaken the mutant. SCOPE: only the files below carry named mutants, and for each only the guards listed; the other mutation=false python files of critical-set.json are covered by their own suites alone (the kill table lists them).
